title: Align subword-mapping and message-framing in onboarding pipeline for versioned models
creator: Jordan Li
description: Summary: During recent onboarding runs for several open checkpoint families we observed subtle divergence between the model-side subword mapping and Redwood's message framing heuristics. This causes off-by-one token counts in prefix caching, inconsistent role delimiters in downstream templates, and degraded perf-profile measurements, which in turn blocks stable version pin publishing. Goals: 1) build a small adapter layer in the onboarding pipeline that normalizes subword boundary mapping into a canonical token map for the profile publisher; 2) make message-framing rules (role/assistant/system delimiters and whitespace heuristics) explicit and pluggable per-model-version so pinned versions keep deterministic tokenization; 3) add gating to the perf profile publisher so profiles with >1% token-count variance are flagged for manual review. Constraints: must be non-disruptive to existing hosted traffic, keep runtime SLOs, and be reversible. Acceptance criteria: - Onboarding runs for 3 representative models produce identical token counts to model-local tokenizer within 0.5% on our test corpus. - Version-pinned models publish a perf profile only after passing the gating checks. - No production latency regressions attributable to the adapter in end-to-end smoke stacks.
comments: 2026-03-02: Created ticket after triage; observed regression during runtime-1.19 rollout on canary. Assigned to Aisha. Initial plan: prototype adapter in onboarding shim and add gating to publisher.

2026-03-04: Spike complete — prototype shim (python) that re-hashes model tokenizer tokenization to Redwood canonical representation. Found three framing cases: trailing newline handling, role delimiter variants, and subtoken merging on punctuation. Notes saved to Confluence.

2026-03-06: Design review with PM and Runtime Eng. Decided to: (a) keep adapter lightweight and optional, (b) expose framing rules in profile metadata, (c) default to strict matching for pinned releases. PM (Carlos Mendes) requested a fallback path for legacy pinned models.

2026-03-08: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-onboard/pull/412 — implements adapter and unit tests. Early benchmarks: onboarding CPU overhead ~6% for our small test suite; KV cache behavior unchanged. Requesting runtime review from @michael.hsu.

2026-03-10: Feedback from runtime review: prefer moving critical normalization logic into the Rust profile publisher for safety and performance. Re-architecting: keep Python shim for experimentation, but port core normalizer to publisher module before merge.

2026-03-12: QA matrix created — three corpora (chatty, instruction-only, long-context) with expected token deltas. Added regression test harness to CI (integration job: onboard-compat-check). Failures currently limited to one model family with aggressive subtoken merges.

2026-03-14: Implementation status: Python shim merged to feature branch, Rust port 60% complete. Added gating rule in publisher: profiles with token-count variance >1% or delimiter mismatch now set status=needs-review and are not auto-published. Next: finish Rust port, run end-to-end canary, and prepare rollout plan for runtime-1.20.
FOLLOWUPS: - Add telemetry to Console for token-count variance at token-level granularity. - Coordinate with devtools to ensure SDK debug mode surfaces framing hints.

REVIEW NOTES: - Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/12456/Subword+Adapter+Design - Runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-runtime/pull/218 - Onboard PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-onboard/pull/412
